title: Go: State Management Store
description: Build a Redux-inspired state store in Go with reducers, middleware chains, selectors, and time-travel debugging.

steps.title: Store with state and reducer
steps.description: Implement a `Store` struct with `state interface{}`, `reducer func(state, action interface{}) interface{}`, and a subscriber system. Implement `Dispatch(action)` that calls the reducer, updates state, and notifies subscribers via channels. Create a counter reducer and print state after dispatching INCREMENT and DECREMENT actions.
hints: Define action types: `type Action struct { Type string; Payload interface{} }`
Dispatch updates state: `s.state = s.reducer(s.state, action)` then notify subscribers
Subscribers receive state via `chan interface{}` — use a goroutine to send

verification.successMessage: Store correctly dispatches actions through the reducer and updates state!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'state: <value>' after each dispatch showing the state change.

steps.title: Dispatch with typed actions
steps.description: Define typed action constants and action creators. Implement a todos reducer that handles ADD_TODO, TOGGLE_TODO, and DELETE_TODO actions. The state is a Todo slice. Dispatch several actions and print the todo list state after each one.
hints: The reducer returns a new state — copy the slice before modifying

verification.successMessage: Typed actions and reducer correctly manage a todo list state!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Todos: <state>' after each dispatch showing the updated state.

steps.title: Middleware type and chain
steps.description: Define a `Middleware` type: `type Middleware func(store *Store, next func(action interface{})) func(action interface{})`. Implement a `Logger` middleware that prints action type and state before/after. Implement `ApplyMiddleware(store, middlewares...)` that composes the middleware chain. Print the logger output.
hints: Middleware wraps Dispatch — each middleware calls next(action) to continue the chain
Logger middleware: print action.Type before next, state after next

verification.successMessage: Middleware chain correctly wraps dispatch with logger instrumentation!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Action: <type> before: <state>' and 'after: <state>' for each dispatch.

steps.title: Async middleware
steps.description: Implement an `AsyncMiddleware` that handles actions with a Promise-like payload. When an action type is ASYNC_START, it executes the payload function in a goroutine and dispatches ASYNC_SUCCESS or ASYNC_FAILURE on completion. Use a simple counter with async increment to demonstrate.
hints: The async middleware intercepts ASYNC_START, launches `go fn()` and dispatches success/failure
Print 'Async started' and 'Async completed' with the result

verification.successMessage: Async middleware handles async actions with goroutines and dispatches results!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Async started' when async action begins and 'Async completed' when finished.

steps.title: Selectors and time-travel debugging
steps.description: Implement a `Selector` type: `type Selector func(state interface{}) interface{}`. Create selectors like `GetTodos`, `GetCompletedCount`. Then implement time-travel by storing a history of states. Add `Undo()` and `Redo()` methods that navigate the history. Print history size and navigate back and forth through states.
hints: History stores `[]interface{}` of past states with a current position index
`Undo` decrements position, `Redo` increments — dispatch appends and resets future
Print history: `fmt.Printf("History: %d states at position %d\n", len(h.states), h.pos)`

verification.successMessage: Selectors extract derived data and time-travel debugging navigates state history!
verification.failureMessage: Print the current state after Undo and Redo showing correct state restoration.
